findings.conditional_on: an administrator delegated one integration permission family to a role that lacks the other
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 6.0): Rocket.Chat splits integration management into two permission families, incoming (webhooks that post into rooms) and outgoing (webhooks that send room traffic to a URL), and the update path decides which object to act on from the type in the request body while loading the stored document by id alone. A holder of manage-incoming-integrations therefore calls integrations.update with type webhook-incoming and an outgoing integration's id, and rewrites that outgoing integration: its target URL, its watched rooms and its script. Because the compiled script is saved before validateChannelRecords runs, even a request that is rejected afterwards leaves the replaced script in place. The attacker gains the other family's capability, which for an outgoing integration is a continuous feed of the watched rooms' messages to a URL they choose, and the symmetric ability to delete the other family's integrations.
findings.remediation: Load the stored document with its type in every query: { _id, type: 'webhook-incoming' } in the incoming updater and its delete, { _id, type: 'webhook-outgoing' } in the outgoing ones (updateIncomingIntegration.ts:101-110, updateOutgoingIntegration.ts:24-32, Integrations.ts:48-60), and move saveCompiledIntegrationScript after every validation so a rejected update cannot write the script. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.md (Validate the Permissions on Every Request) and deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Insecure_Direct_Object_Reference_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.md (resolve the object within what the caller may reach).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps both integration features and removes only the weakness: a request naming the wrong type fails with an invalid-integration error (the admin UI never sends one), and a rejected update leaves the stored script untouched, so a client that relied on the partial write to stage a script must send a valid request.

findings.title: Revoking preview-c-room only closes the history and the live stream: ten other message, file and thread routes still serve non-members
findings.category: Authorization missing on alternate API routes
findings.status: CONFIRMED (with preview-c-room revoked, 4 other route(s) (channels.messages, chat.syncMessages, chat.getMessage, chat.search) still served the channel's messages to a non-member while channels.history and the stream refused it)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven by our own run against the pinned build; needs an account, a non-default feature.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 07 F-62: searched preview-c-room removed channels.messages still readable non-member; adjacent only PRs #34922 and #35194 (the stream side).
findings.conditional_on: an administrator removed preview-c-room from a role (a hardening control switched on but enforced on two read paths only)
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 4.3): preview-c-room is the permission an administrator removes to stop people reading public channels they have not joined. The rule lives in canReadRoom, which adds the preview test on top of canAccessRoom, and only two paths use it: the channel-history method and the room-message stream. Every other read of the same content calls canAccessRoom, which admits any view-c-room holder to a public channel, so after the revocation a non-member still reads the channel through channels.messages, chat.syncMessages, chat.getMessage, chat.search, the thread routes, pins, discussions, files and images. The administrator sees the timeline close in the web client and has no indication that the API never closed.
findings.remediation: Make the preview rule the shared predicate rather than a special case: replace canAccessRoomAsync with canReadRoom (or introduce canReadRoomMessages and use it) in each message, file and thread read that currently calls canAccessRoom, starting with channels.messages (channels.ts:522), channels.files (channels.ts:1181), getSingleMessage.ts:14 and the chat.ts sync, search and thread routes. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.md (Validate the Permissions on Every Request, through one shared decision point).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps public channels exactly as they behave by default (preview-c-room is on the user role, so nothing changes until an administrator revokes it) and removes only the weakness: once revoked, non-members lose these reads as they already lost the history, and holders of the permission see no difference.

findings.title: On a fresh install the REST API has no per-route rate limiting until the server restarts, and changes to the default limit never apply
findings.category: Missing rate limiting
findings.status: CONFIRMED (4 ordinary GET routes accepted 25 calls each with the documented limit at 10 per 60000 ms, and lowering the default to 2 changed nothing: the default rule is never registered)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven by our own run against the pinned build; unauthenticated, default configuration.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 07 F-63: adjacent PR #13451 ('Restart required to apply changes in API Rate Limiter settings', 2019: the second leg regresses it), issue #13441, open issue #43048 / PR #43050.
findings.impact: While it lasts, nothing at the REST layer bounds attempts on any route; administrators' changes to the default limit are ignored.
findings.remediation: Read the default limits when a rule is created or checked, keep one shared options object, and store the HTTP method so reloads re-register <route><verb>.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps the limiter and makes it work as documented; clients over a route's limit get 429 on a fresh install too.
findings.detail: Filtered (rate limiting): route limiters are built from a module-load snapshot of the default settings (ApiClass.ts:151-154) and re-registered under '<route>action' names (:504-518), so a fresh install has no per-route REST limits until it restarts and an administrator's change to the default never applies: a regression of PR #13451 (stage 08 R-18). Missing rate limiting is out of scope by policy, but a human may override that here because the product documents the protection as present.

findings.title: Apps marketplace REST routes have no manage-apps check, so any user obtains a workspace Cloud token with purchase scope
findings.category: Missing authorization (server credential exposed)
findings.status: NEEDS_MANUAL (the marketplace routes need a Cloud-registered workspace, which a sealed unlicensed lab does not have)
findings.confidence_reasoning: The mechanism is clear in source; the lab could not complete the trigger, so a person has to finish it.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 07 F-64: searched buildExternalUrl marketplace token manage-apps; adjacent CVE-2026-55762 (fingerprint without authorization, fixed 8.5.1) and CVE-2026-23477. Stage 08 R-22: residual of CVE-2026-29197 (GHSA-37hj-44gj-w9gc), whose fix put manage-apps on the log routes only.
findings.conditional_on: the workspace registered with Rocket.Chat Cloud
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 5.4): buildExternalUrl is declared with authRequired only, and it mints a workspace Cloud access token through the client_credentials grant using the workspace's Cloud client id and secret, with scope marketplace:purchase, then returns it inside a URL in the response body. Any signed-in user therefore extracts a bearer token that speaks for the whole workspace to Rocket.Chat Cloud, together with the workspace id and the active-user count. The app-request routes beside it proxy with the same credential, so the same caller reads which apps colleagues asked administrators to install, with requester details, and can mark those requests seen, which corrupts an administrator workflow. What the token is worth on the Cloud side cannot be established from the lab, which is why this needs a registered workspace to settle.
findings.remediation: Add permissionsRequired: ['manage-apps'] to buildExternalUrl, app-request, app-request/stats and app-request/markAsSeen in ee/server/api/apps/rest.ts; and stop returning the token at all: have the server open the purchase session (or issue a short-lived, single-use redirect) so a workspace credential never reaches a browser or a response body. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.md (Enforce Least Privileges) and deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.md (a server credential is never handed to a client).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps the marketplace flow and removes only the weakness: non-administrators lose two routes the admin UI never offers them, the request flow (buildExternalAppRequest and the notify-admins path) is unchanged, and an administrator's purchase journey gains one server-side redirect instead of a token-bearing URL.

findings.title: HEAD requests run the GET handler but are counted under a limiter name that is never registered, so every GET route's rate limit, and per-method parameter validation, is skipped
findings.category: Rate-limit bypass (verb tampering)
findings.status: FAILED (HEAD took 20 calls with 0 refusals against 0 for GET, so the limiter key does ignore HEAD; filtered under the rate-limit rule, and the per-verb validation leg needs a human route by route)
findings.confidence_reasoning: HEAD is genuinely not counted, but on this build the default rule is not registered for GET either, so nothing was being enforced to bypass.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 07 F-65: searched HEAD request bypass rate limit GET route Hono; OSV hono@4.13.13: 5 advisories fixed in 4.13.16, none about HEAD or limiter keys; adjacent only hono issues #5506 and #1130.
findings.impact: HEAD bypasses every GET route's declared limit; for routes that declare validateParams per verb, the GET handler runs on unvalidated input.
findings.remediation: Compute the limiter name and the validateParams key from the handler's method (treat HEAD as GET), or reject HEAD on routes that do not declare it.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps HEAD support; HEAD requests count against the GET budget.
findings.detail: Filtered (rate-limit bypass), with one leg left open: the limiter key is built from the request verb (ApiClass.ts:794-797), so a HEAD request, which Hono routes to the GET handler, matches no rule and escapes every GET route's declared limit. The leg for a human is that per-verb validateParams is looked up by the same verb (:809-819), so a GET handler whose schema is declared per method (livechat/message/:_id, for one) runs on unvalidated query input under HEAD; a HEAD response has no body, so the impact depends on each handler's side effects, route by route.

findings.title: Disabling password reset closes only the REST route: Meteor's forgotPassword still mails reset links anonymously and outside the REST limiter
findings.category: Feature switch not enforced on an alternate channel
findings.status: CONFIRMED (with self-service password reset switched off, an unauthenticated caller still had the workspace mail a working reset link, through the method bridge and outside the REST limiter)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven: with reset switched off, an anonymous caller still had a working reset link mailed, outside the REST limiter.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 07 F-66: searched forgotPassword method Accounts_PasswordReset disabled; adjacent only GHSA-7c6v-m68v-v73r / CVE-2026-75575 (sendForgotPasswordEmail without a DDP rate limit, fixed 8.8.0), issue #9434, CVE-2020-28208.
findings.conditional_on: Accounts_PasswordReset turned off (self-service reset disabled, a switch that is then not fully enforced)
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 4.8): Accounts_PasswordReset is the switch an administrator turns off when passwords are managed elsewhere (an identity team, an SSO-only workspace) so that nobody can mail themselves a reset link. The switch is read in the REST route users.forgotPassword and in the login form, not in the capability: Meteor's own forgotPassword handler looks the account up and mails the token with no Rocket.Chat check, and it is reachable over DDP and through POST /api/v1/method.callAnon/forgotPassword, a route that is anonymous and explicitly opts out of the REST rate limiter. So every account remains resettable by whoever controls its mailbox, and anyone can make the workspace send reset mail to any address at a pace only the DDP limiter bounds, while the administrator believes the feature is off.
findings.remediation: Enforce the switch in the capability rather than in one route: wrap Meteor's forgotPassword and resetPassword handlers so they refuse while Accounts_PasswordReset is false, or refuse those method names in method.call, method.callAnon and the DDP dispatcher when the switch is off; the same wrapper is where the policy and second-factor gaps in the sibling finding belong. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Forgot_Password_Cheat_Sheet.md (the recovery flow is one capability, gated in one place) and deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.md (Validate the Permissions on Every Request).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps password reset working when it is enabled and removes only the weakness: with the switch off no reset mail can be requested over any channel, which is what the switch states, so a workspace that quietly relied on the Meteor method (no first-party client does) loses it.

findings.title: channels.list sorts on client-chosen fields before projecting, so a join code is recoverable by bisection
findings.category: Sort oracle on a hidden field
findings.status: CONFIRMED (recovered a 5-character join code exactly in 58 requests from the sort order alone, and joined the channel it protected)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven by our own run against the pinned build; needs an account, default configuration.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 07 F-67: searched channels.list sort joinCode hidden field oracle; adjacent only PR #8420 (field and query restrictions that do not cover sort) and PR #41948. Stage 08 R-27 links it to the CVE-2022-32219 fix that removed client queries but left sort keys.
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 4.3): the channel listing passes the caller's sort straight to MongoDB, which orders the matched documents before the projection removes non-public fields. joinCode, the plain-text code that gates joining a protected public channel, is one of those fields: it is withheld from the response and still sortable. A user who can create channels sets a join code on a probe channel of their own, asks for the list sorted by joinCode, and reads from the target's position relative to the probe whether the target's code sorts before or after theirs. Repeating with adjusted probe values recovers the target's code character by character, after which the attacker joins a channel whose owners deliberately gated membership.
findings.remediation: Give parseJsonQuery a per-route allow-list of sortable fields (the ones each listing actually projects) and reject anything else with a 400 rather than passing it to Mongo, in parseJsonQuery.ts:16-37 and at the call site in channels.ts:1434. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Input_Validation_Cheat_Sheet.md (validate against an allow-list when the value space is known) with deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Error_Handling_Cheat_Sheet.md for not letting ordering answer questions the response does not.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps sorting for the fields the listings return and removes only the weakness: an API client that sorted on a field outside the allow-list receives a 400 instead of a privileged ordering, so a custom client sorting on an internal field must change.

findings.title: rooms.bannedUsers returns a room's ban list to any member, while the client shows it only to holders of ban-user
findings.category: Missing authorization on a moderation view
findings.status: CONFIRMED (an ordinary member and a non-member both read the room's banned-user list, which the interface shows only to holders of ban-user)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven by our own run against the pinned build; needs an account, default configuration.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 07 F-68: searched rooms.bannedUsers permission ban-user any member list; adjacent only PR #43138 (9.0 returns 403 for no room access) and PR #41402.
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 4.3): the route's only gate is canAccessRoomIdAsync, so anyone who can open the room receives the banned members' user ids, usernames and display names. The client puts the same data behind a permission: the room-toolbox action that opens the Banned Users panel returns nothing unless usePermission('ban-user', room._id) holds, so in the interface the list is a moderators' view. Moderation decisions are personal and often deliberately quiet (who was removed from an incident room, who was banned after a complaint), and here every member of the room, and for a public channel every user who can see it, can enumerate them.
findings.remediation: Check the same permission the client checks, scoped to the room: in rooms.ts:1749 require hasPermissionAsync(this.userId, 'ban-user', roomId) in addition to room access, mirroring useBannedUsersRoomAction.ts:12-17. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.md (Enforce Least Privileges, and Verify that Authorization Checks are Performed in the Right Location: the server, not the toolbox).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps the list for moderators and administrators and removes only the weakness: ordinary members receive 403 for a panel the interface never offered them, so a third-party client that displayed the ban list to everyone will show an error instead.

findings.title: Removing the admin role skips assign-admin-role: users.update replaces the role list with no last-admin guard
findings.category: Role hierarchy not enforced
findings.status: CONFIRMED (a delegate refused the promotion guard still removed the admin role from an administrator through users.update, which the sibling route refuses)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven by our own run against the pinned build; needs an account, a non-default feature.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 07 F-69: searched roles.removeUserFromRole admin assign-admin-role users.update roles last admin; adjacent only PR #22949 (last-admin deactivation guard; a reviewer asked for the same on role removal) and PR #42947.
findings.conditional_on: an administrator delegated role management without assign-admin-role
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 6.5): granting the admin role requires assign-admin-role (validateUserData refuses a roles array containing admin without it, and the add-to-role method does the same), but taking it away requires neither that permission nor any equivalent. users.update sets the whole roles array through updater.set('roles', userData.roles) behind assign-roles alone, with no admin-specific check and no last-admin guard, so a delegated role manager demotes administrators one by one and can leave the workspace with none. roles.removeUserFromRole is gated only on access-permissions; it does keep one admin, which is the guard the users.update path lacks entirely. The product's role hierarchy therefore holds for promotions and not for demotions.
findings.remediation: Apply the same rule in both directions: require assign-admin-role whenever admin is removed from or absent in a submitted roles array (extend the check in validateUserData.ts:78 to compare the submitted list with the stored one), and add the last-admin guard that roles.removeUserFromRole has (roles.ts:299-304) to the saveUser path so no route can remove the final administrator. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.md (Enforce Least Privileges; a role-management permission must not reach above itself).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps delegated role management and removes only the weakness: a manager without assign-admin-role can no longer demote administrators (they can still manage every other role), and no path can remove the last administrator, so a workspace that deliberately demoted its final admin through the API must now use the console or keep one.

findings.title: autotranslate.translateMessage omits the auto-translate permission its sibling routes and the client require
findings.category: Missing permission check on one of three twin routes
findings.status: CONFIRMED (an account without the auto-translate permission reached translateMessage, which its sibling route refuses it, and the handler ran to the provider)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven by our own run against the pinned build; needs an account, a non-default feature.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 07 F-70: parent CVE-2026-32994 (HackerOne #3713682, the route returned any message by id; fixed 8.5.0 by PR #40508, which added only canAccessRoomAsync); also CVE-2026-32995 (DDP method). The missing permission is not reported.
findings.conditional_on: AutoTranslate_Enabled with a translation provider configured
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 4.3): auto-translate is an administrator-held permission (it is created with roles ['admin']) and the other server functions in the feature check it: getSupportedLanguages and saveSettings both refuse a caller without it, and the web client checks it before using the feature at all. The on-demand translation route does not: it verifies the feature switch and the caller's access to the message's room, and then calls the configured provider. So any authenticated user makes the workspace's paid translation provider process any message they can open, as often as they like, which spends the organisation's per-character budget and sends that message's text to the third-party provider on the initiative of a user the administrator excluded from the feature.
findings.remediation: Declare the permission on the route: add permissionsRequired: ['auto-translate'] to autotranslate.translateMessage (autotranslate.ts:156-172), or perform an explicit hasPermissionAsync(this.userId, 'auto-translate') check in the handler before calling translateMessage, matching getSupportedLanguages.ts:12 and saveSettings.ts:14. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.md (Validate the Permissions on Every Request) with deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Denial_of_Service_Cheat_Sheet.md for the metered-resource angle.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps translation for the users an administrator permitted and removes only the weakness: a user without auto-translate loses on-demand translation, which the client already hides from them, so no first-party flow changes.

findings.title: e2e.fetchUsersWaitingForGroupKey takes room ids from the caller without authorizing them, disclosing private rooms' members
findings.category: Object reference not authorized (membership disclosure)
findings.status: CONFIRMED (a non-member listed an encrypted private group's waiting members and their keys through a route that authorises no room id)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven by our own run against the pinned build; needs an account, a non-default feature.
findings.known_evidence: Fix PR #41953 'fix: check room access in e2e.fetchUsersWaitingForGroupKey' (opened 2026-08-26, open, unmerged) describes this endpoint and root cause; e2e.ts:363-368 unchanged at 9f3d6c8c. No advisory. https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/pull/41953
findings.conditional_on: E2E_Enable (end-to-end encryption) enabled
findings.impact: Low (CVSS 3.1): the route reads roomIds straight from the query string and passes them to an aggregation that matches any subscription whose rid is in that list, excluding only the caller's own. So a user who knows a private room's id receives up to fifty of its members' user ids and end-to-end public keys, without being in the room. Its twin method, e2e.getUsersOfRoomWithoutKey, authorizes the room first with canAccessRoomIdAsync, which shows the intended rule. The disclosure is partial membership (the members still waiting for the room key) rather than content, and it needs the room id, which is why this is Low.
findings.remediation: Authorize each requested room before the aggregation: keep only the ids where the caller holds a subscription carrying the room key (or call canAccessRoomIdAsync per id, as getUsersOfRoomWithoutKey.ts:11 does) in e2e.ts:362-370, and let the model method keep its current shape. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Insecure_Direct_Object_Reference_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.md (resolve objects within what the caller may reach).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps end-to-end key distribution working and removes only the weakness: no first-party client behaviour changes, because the client only ever sends the ids of rooms the user is in; a caller asking about a room it cannot access gets that room omitted from the response.

findings.title: Turning off personal data export (UserData_EnableDownload) only blocks the download link: users.requestDataDownload and the export cron still build and mail archives
findings.category: Feature switch enforced in one channel only
findings.status: FAILED (the archive was built and its link mailed with exports switched off, but the download is refused, so nothing leaves the server: filtered as informational, exactly as the report has it)
findings.confidence_reasoning: The mechanism reproduces (the archive is built and mailed with exports off) but the download is refused, so nothing leaves the server.
findings.known_evidence: Issue #17199 'User Data Download disabled - cron still working' (2020-04-07; closed 2020-06-26 by the stale bot, no fix); the request route and the cron still ignore the switch in this build. https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/issues/17199
findings.impact: With exports off, the server still builds archives and mails links that the download route then refuses.
findings.remediation: Check the switch in requestDataDownload and in the cron.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps exports when enabled; with the switch off requests are refused at the start.
findings.detail: Filtered (informational): with UserData_EnableDownload off, users.requestDataDownload and the export cron still build the archive and mail the link, because userDataDownload.ts:57-62 is the only place the switch is read, but that route then refuses the download, so storage and CPU are spent and no data leaves the server. Publicly known as issue #17199, closed by a stale bot without a fix.

findings.title: Mailer placeholder regex is still quadratic after the CVE-2021-32832 fix, and the anonymous offline form feeds it unbounded text
findings.category: Denial of service (regular expression complexity, ReDoS)
findings.status: CONFIRMED (an unauthenticated request held the server for 20.02s at 80000 characters, the cost growing 44.5x for 16x the input)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven unauthenticated: one request held the workspace for twenty seconds and the cost grew quadratically.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 08 R-03: parent GHSA-wpp8-mvvg-33rx / CVE-2021-32832 (GHSL-2020-310, fixed 3.11.3, 3.12.2, 3.13 by commit 4a0dce9, which replaced the exponential pattern with a quadratic one); vendor-tracker searches 'replaceVariables regex' and 'offline.message ReDoS': 0 results.
findings.impact: High (CVSS 7.5): replaceVariables runs /\{ *([^\{\} ]+)[^\{\}]*\}/gim over every string the mailer templates, and the two adjacent negated character classes overlap, so an opening brace followed by a long run of non-brace characters with no closing brace makes the engine try every split: quadratic work per brace, on the single thread that serves the whole workspace. The anonymous Livechat offline form reaches it with no length bound: its schema declares name, email and message as plain strings with no maxLength, and Mailer.send evaluates replace() on the subject and twice on the HTML body (for the text part and for wrap) before sendNoWrap even looks at the recipient, so no offline recipient needs to be configured for the work to happen. One unauthenticated request per five seconds per address is enough to hold the event loop.
findings.remediation: Make the scan linear rather than regex-backtracked in replaceVariables.ts:1-2 (find a brace, read the key up to a space or a closing brace, give up at the next opening brace), and bound the inputs: add maxLength to name, email and message in the offline-message schema (rest-typings omnichannel.ts:2349-2372) and cap the strings the mailer will template at a few kilobytes. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Denial_of_Service_Cheat_Sheet.md (validate input size; bound the work per request) with deploy/knowledge/payloads/PayloadsAllTheThings/Regular Expression/README.md for the pattern shapes.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps mail templating and the offline form and removes only the weakness: an offline message longer than the cap is refused with a 400, and templates with well-formed placeholders behave exactly as before (a malformed, unclosed brace is simply left as text, as it is today).

findings.title: Unbounded metric label cardinality: method.call samples are labelled with the raw request path, so anonymous requests grow the registry until memory runs out
findings.category: Uncontrolled resource consumption (unbounded metric label cardinality)
findings.status: CONFIRMED (300 anonymous requests with distinct paths added 7774 time series and grew the metrics body by 1024449 bytes, with nothing evicting them)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven with the metrics endpoint on: 300 anonymous requests doubled the registry and nothing evicts the series.
findings.known_evidence: Not covered by any stage 07 search (the pointer came from stage 05); no advisory or issue names metrics label growth in Rocket.Chat; searching for it is left to stage 12.
findings.impact: High (CVSS 7.5): the REST metrics middleware normally labels a sample with the matched route pattern, which is a bounded set, but for any route whose pattern starts with method.call it substitutes decodeURIComponent(path), the raw request path. method.callAnon/:method matches any method name, is unauthenticated and explicitly opts out of the REST rate limiter, so each request with a fresh path segment creates a new label set in a prom-client Summary (with percentiles) and in two Histograms (fourteen and nine buckets), which are retained in process memory. The middleware is mounted by startRestAPI whether or not Prometheus is enabled, prom-client imposes no cardinality cap, and Prometheus_Reset_Interval ships at 0, so nothing ever clears them: an anonymous attacker with throughput grows the registry until the container's memory limit is reached and the process dies.
findings.remediation: Label method-bridge samples with something bounded: use the route pattern, or the method name when it resolves to a registered Meteor method and the literal unknown otherwise, instead of decodeURIComponent(path) at metrics.ts:57; and cap the number of distinct label values the middleware will create per metric, dropping to a catch-all label beyond it. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Denial_of_Service_Cheat_Sheet.md (bound the resources one request may allocate) with deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.md for not letting request data shape the telemetry.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps the metrics and removes only the weakness: per-path series for method-bridge calls collapse into one series per method name (or into unknown for unregistered names), so a dashboard that counted invalid method paths individually loses that detail; valid method metrics are unchanged.

findings.title: Pending-file importer fetches export-supplied URLs with Node's raw HTTP client, bypassing the SSRF guard its sibling fetch now uses
findings.category: Server-side request forgery (non-blind, privileged importer)
findings.status: NEEDS_MANUAL (the pending-file record has to be seeded beside the run and that did not fit this stage's time budget)
findings.confidence_reasoning: The mechanism is clear in source; the lab could not complete the trigger, so a person has to finish it.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 08 R-04: parent GHSA-6x96-99rg-wg67 (blind SSRF in downloadPublicImportFile; < 8.8.0 and backports; fixed by PR #41749, which changed only that file); vendor-tracker search 'PendingFileImporter' returned 16 items, none about SSRF. https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/security/advisories/GHSA-6x96-99rg-wg67
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 6.8): the Slack importer records each message attachment's url_private_download from the uploaded export as the pending file's download URL, and downloadPendingFiles fetches it with Node's own http/https client rather than @rocket.chat/server-fetch, so neither the SSRF guard nor SSRF_Allowlist applies. Whatever answers with a 2xx is stored through fileStore._doInsert, which the code comments note bypasses the file-store filters, and attached to the imported message as a downloadable file. So a holder of run-import who uploads a crafted export makes the server request arbitrary internal URLs from its own network position and reads the responses back out of the workspace: a non-blind SSRF, against exactly the hosts the guard and the allow-list exist to protect.
findings.remediation: Fetch through the guarded client in PendingFileImporter.downloadFile (PendingFileImporter.ts:164-195): use fetch from @rocket.chat/server-fetch with ignoreSsrfValidation: false and allowList: settings.get('SSRF_Allowlist'), exactly as the sibling import fetch does after the GHSA-6x96 fix, and accept only http(s) URLs on the export's expected hosts. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.md (validate the destination, use one guarded client) with deploy/knowledge/payloads/PayloadsAllTheThings/Server Side Request Forgery/README.md for the internal targets to test.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps pending-file imports from public hosts and removes only the weakness: a file hosted on an internal address is no longer fetched unless an administrator allow-lists it, so an on-premises export whose attachments sit on an internal file server needs that host added to SSRF_Allowlist.

findings.title: Livechat stream access is decided against the room the client names in extraData, so a visitor with one open chat of its own reads any other Livechat room's live messages
findings.category: Broken access control (authorization decided on a client-chosen object)
findings.status: CONFIRMED (an unauthenticated visitor subscribed to another customer's Livechat room by naming its own room in extraData and received that customer's messages)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven unauthenticated: naming our own room in extraData opened another customer's live conversation.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 08 R-01: regression of CVE-2026-48616 (Livechat file access decided on a client-supplied room); the stream path keeps the same pattern; no tracker or advisory names the room-messages stream.
findings.conditional_on: Livechat_enabled (Omnichannel on), with the attacker able to open one chat of its own
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 5.9): the stream-room-messages read rule passes the subscriber's own subscription arguments to canReadRoom as extraData, and for a Livechat room the third compatibility validator reloads LivechatRooms.findOneById(extraData.rid) and overwrites the room under test with it before comparing the visitor token. So an anonymous visitor who opens one chat of their own, and who knows a target room's id, subscribes to that target room and is authorized against their own: the server then pushes the other customer's conversation to them live. The same client-supplied-room pattern was the subject of CVE-2026-48616 on the file-access path; on the realtime path it is still there.
findings.remediation: Compare the visitor token against the room actually being accessed. In roomAccessValidator.compatibility.ts:30-39, drop the extraData.rid reload and return extraData?.visitorToken && room.v?.token === extraData.visitorToken && room.open === true, refusing outright when extraData.rid is present and differs from room._id; give the upload path that genuinely has no room object its own validator that resolves the room from the upload record instead of from the client. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Insecure_Direct_Object_Reference_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.md (Mitigation: authorize the object being accessed) and deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.md (Validate the Permissions on Every Request).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps visitor streams for the visitor's own rooms and removes only the weakness: a subscription that names a different room in extraData.rid than the one it subscribes to is refused, which no first-party widget does.

findings.title: livechat/visitors.pagesVisited returns navigation messages whole, handing any agent the visitor tokens the GHSA-cqj7 fix stopped visitors.info from disclosing
findings.category: Credential disclosure (missing projection and room authorization)
findings.status: CONFIRMED (a non-admin agent read the customer's visitor token out of visitors.pagesVisited, which visitors.info withholds for the same caller, and used it to read the conversation and post as the customer)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven: the token visitors.info withholds came out of the sibling route and then read and wrote the conversation.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 08 R-02: regression of GHSA-cqj7-h8cj-jmf2 / CVE-2026-49278 (visitors.info returned the visitor token; fixed 8.5.0, 8.4.2 and backports by projecting token: 0); vendor-tracker search 'pagesVisited token' returned only test PRs #42534 and #39419. https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/security/advisories/GHSA-cqj7-h8cj-jmf2
findings.conditional_on: Livechat_enabled (Omnichannel on)
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 5.4): the route is gated on view-l-room alone, and findVisitedPages loads any Livechat room by the id in the URL, performs no room-access check, and returns its livechat_navigation_history messages with no projection. Each of those messages was written by the widget with the visitor's own token inside navigation.token, so the response hands the caller the credential that authenticates that customer. With it, an agent of one department reads another department's conversation through livechat/messages.history and posts into it as the customer through livechat/message. That is the impersonation GHSA-cqj7-h8cj-jmf2 was issued for, through a second endpoint the fix did not touch.
findings.remediation: Authorize the room and withhold the token in findVisitedPages (lib/visitors.ts:26-36): call canAccessRoomAsync for the requesting user as the sibling findChatHistory does at :61, and pass projection: { 'navigation.token': 0 } to findPaginatedByRoomIdAndType; better still, stop writing the token into the navigation message at tracking.ts:35-38, since the room already records the visitor. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Authorization_Cheat_Sheet.md (Validate the Permissions on Every Request) with deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Session_Management_Cheat_Sheet.md (a session identifier is never disclosed to a third party).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps the navigation-history panel and removes only the weakness: agents see page history for the rooms they can access rather than for every room, and the token no longer appears in the response, which the first-party agent UI never reads.

findings.title: The DDP-over-REST bridges key their rate limits on the caller's own X-Auth-Token header, so every header-less anonymous caller shares one bucket and a rotating header escapes it
findings.category: Denial of service through a shared rate-limit key (and limit bypass)
findings.status: CONFIRMED (one anonymous client exhausted the bucket every other anonymous client shares, and rotating the X-Auth-Token header escaped the limit entirely)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven: one anonymous client's burst had an unrelated anonymous client refused, and a rotated header escaped the limit.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 08 R-06: residual of RCSA-2023-0004 (vendor security page; rate-limiter bypass by modifying User-Agent, fixed 6.5.1 with an IP fallback that is now dead code); vendor-tracker search 'method.callAnon rate limit' found nothing about the key. https://docs.rocket.chat/docs/security-fixes-and-updates
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 5.3): ApiClass sets this.token = hashLoginToken(String(authToken)) on every REST request, so with no X-Auth-Token header it becomes the hash of the string null, a constant. Both method bridges then compute connectionId = this.token || sha256(ip), which means the IP fallback never runs and every header-less anonymous caller is counted as the same DDP connection. Meteor's default accounts rule allows five login, createUser, resetPassword or forgotPassword calls per connection per ten seconds, and the web client sends every password login through method.callAnon with no auth header, so five anonymous login calls every ten seconds make every logged-out user's web login fail with too-many-requests, workspace-wide. The same key, being caller-chosen, works the other way too: a fresh random X-Auth-Token per request gives each one its own bucket and lifts the per-connection limits on anonymous login and forgotPassword guessing.
findings.remediation: Key the limiter on something the caller cannot choose. In ApiClass.ts:791-792 leave this.token undefined when the header is absent (hash only a header that is actually present), and in the two bridges (misc.ts:642-647 and :687-692) key anonymous calls on this.requestIp and authenticated calls on this.userId rather than on a header hash. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Denial_of_Service_Cheat_Sheet.md (Rate limiting: the key must identify the client, not be supplied by it) with deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.md (Account Lockout).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps both bridges and their limits, and removes only the weakness: limits become per client address for anonymous calls and per user for authenticated ones, so one client can no longer exhaust another's bucket, and a client can no longer reset its own by changing a header. A deployment behind a proxy that does not set a forwarded-for header would see all its users share an address, which is the standard reason to configure the proxy headers Rocket.Chat already documents.

findings.title: getRoomByTypeAndName passes an untyped method parameter into a Mongo filter, so any user enumerates private-room names by regular expression through its two distinct error codes
findings.category: NoSQL operator injection (existence oracle)
findings.status: CONFIRMED (ordinary accounts recovered the exact name of a private group they cannot see ('proj-015b') in 327 oracle questions, through a Mongo operator in a method parameter)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven by our own run against the pinned build; needs an account, default configuration.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 08 R-09: regression of GHSA-jx87-887q-554q / CVE-2022-32226 (getUsersOfRoom input not type validated, fixed 4.8.2; the fix was applied per method); no advisory names getRoomByTypeAndName (tracker search not completed: GitHub search API limit). https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jx87-887q-554q
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 4.3): the Meteor method validates only that type and name are truthy, and for channel and private-group types there is no per-type roomFind, so the parameter reaches Rooms.findByTypeAndNameOrId and is placed into $or: [{ name: identifier }, { _id: identifier }] unchanged. An EJSON object such as {"$regex":"^acq"} therefore becomes a pattern match over every room of that type, and the method's two failure codes tell the caller which happened: error-no-permission when a room matched that the caller may not open, error-invalid-room when nothing matched. Bisecting one character at a time recovers the names of private groups the caller is not a member of, which in practice are project, deal and incident code names.
findings.remediation: Type the parameters and collapse the error codes. At the top of getRoomByTypeAndName (publications/room/index.ts:53-58) add check(type, String) and check(name, String) (or a schema), and return the same error-invalid-room for both no match and no access so the response no longer distinguishes them. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Input_Validation_Cheat_Sheet.md (validate type before use) with the technique in deploy/knowledge/payloads/PayloadsAllTheThings/NoSQL Injection/README.md.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps the method for its real callers and removes only the weakness: a non-string name is refused rather than treated as a query, and a caller can no longer tell a room they may not see from one that does not exist. A client that relied on telling those two cases apart (no first-party client does; the web client treats both as "room not found") would lose that distinction.

findings.title: The Livechat widget composer writes pasted text back into the page as HTML: DOMPurify guards the emoji path but not componentDidUpdate
findings.category: DOM-based XSS (self-XSS in the visitor widget)
findings.status: FAILED (the paste did not execute (pasted=False, dialogs=[]); the composer path was exercised in a real browser)
findings.confidence_reasoning: The composer path was exercised in a real browser and the paste did not execute; the write is there in source, but the guard held in this build.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 08 R-11: regression of GHSA-hf55-c445-2w97 / CVE-2022-21830 (HackerOne #1091118; @rocket.chat/livechat < 1.9.0, fixed by Livechat PR #558 with a DOMPurify sanitize on input); in this monorepo copy the sanitize call survives only on the emoji-insertion path (Composer/index.tsx:218) and the componentDidUpdate write at :204 has none; OSV places @rocket.chat/livechat 3.0.0 past the advisory range, so no tooling flags this build; no advisory or issue names the componentDidUpdate write. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hf55-c445-2w97
findings.conditional_on: Livechat_enabled (Omnichannel on, so the widget can chat)
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 4.2): the composer reads its contents as innerText, hands that decoded text up to ChatFooter, receives it back as the value prop, and in componentDidUpdate assigns it to el.innerHTML whenever it differs from the element's serialised HTML, which it does as soon as the text contains a markup character. DOMPurify is imported in the same file and used on the emoji-insertion path at line 218, so the guard exists and this path simply does not use it. shouldComponentUpdate only lets an update through when the value goes from empty to non-empty, from non-empty to empty, or reaches the character limit, so the trigger is a paste into an empty composer rather than typing: paste and the handler runs in the widget frame on the workspace origin, where the visitor token lives. It is self-XSS, as CVE-2022-21830 was, so the attacker needs the victim to perform the paste.
findings.remediation: Treat the composer's value as text in componentDidUpdate (Composer/index.tsx:196-207): assign el.textContent = this.value, or pass it through the DOMPurify.sanitize already imported in this file and used at :218 if the markup round trip is needed for emoji. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/DOM_based_XSS_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.md (assign untrusted data with textContent rather than innerHTML) with the payloads in deploy/knowledge/payloads/PayloadsAllTheThings/XSS Injection/README.md.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps the composer and removes only the weakness: markup pasted into the message box is shown as the literal characters the visitor pasted, which is what they typed anyway. Emoji insertion keeps its own sanitised path, so the one place that legitimately writes markup (the non-breaking space it inserts after an emoji) is unaffected.

findings.title: The Livechat webhook sender and its test route keep ignoreSsrfValidation on, for the same non-admin Omnichannel roles PR #42201 stopped from reaching internal hosts through triggers
findings.category: Server-side request forgery (privileged Omnichannel role)
findings.status: CONFIRMED (a non-admin livechat-manager made the server fetch URLs of its choosing, including a host only the server can reach, and received the customer's conversation data at its own listener)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven: a non-admin role made the server fetch hosts only it can reach and received customer data at our listener.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 08 R-05: sibling of PR #42201 'fix!: SSRF validation disabled in Livechat trigger external service' (merged 2026-10-26, 9.0.0), which has no CVE or GHSA id; tracker search 'webhook.test SSRF' not completed (GitHub search API limit). https://github.com/RocketChat/Rocket.Chat/pull/42201
findings.conditional_on: Livechat_enabled (Omnichannel on) with a livechat-manager or livechat-monitor account
findings.impact: Medium (CVSS 4.1): a livechat-manager or livechat-monitor sets Livechat_webhookUrl through POST /api/v1/omnichannel/integrations, which requires view-livechat-manager and writes the value after a trim with no scheme or host validation. Both outbound calls that use it pass ignoreSsrfValidation: true to serverFetch, so the SSRF guard and SSRF_Allowlist are skipped: livechat/webhook.test (view-livechat-webhooks) posts sample data and distinguishes a 200 from everything else, which is a probe of any internal address and port the container can reach, and the event sender posts real conversation data to the same URL whenever an enabled Livechat event fires. The vendor removed exactly this opt-out from the Livechat trigger call in PR #42201 for a permission held by the same roles, which is what settles that non-admin Omnichannel roles reaching internal hosts is a bug rather than a feature.
findings.remediation: Remove ignoreSsrfValidation: true from both Livechat webhook fetches (api/v1/omnichannel/webhooks.ts:60-70 and lib/omnichannel/webhooks.ts:23-33) and pass allowList: settings.get('SSRF_Allowlist') instead, exactly as PR #42201 did in ee/server/api/v1/omnichannel/lib/triggers.ts:19-26; validate the configured URL's scheme when it is set in integration.ts:28-32, and return one indistinguishable result from the test route so it cannot serve as a port oracle. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.md (allow-list the destination; do not report the outcome back to the requester).
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps Livechat webhooks working for public receivers and removes only the weakness: a receiver on an internal address stops working until an administrator adds it to SSRF_Allowlist, which is a real behaviour change for on-premises deployments whose webhook consumer sits beside the app, and the test route's answer becomes less informative about why a receiver failed.

findings.title: CVE-2025-5892's IRC parser ReDoS is unfixed in this build: the quadratic whitespace expression is unchanged and the proposed fix was never merged
findings.category: Denial of service (regular expression complexity, ReDoS)
findings.status: NEEDS_MANUAL (the IRC parser is only reachable from an IRC peer, which this sealed lab does not provide)
findings.confidence_reasoning: The mechanism is clear in source; the lab could not complete the trigger, so a person has to finish it.
findings.known_evidence: GHSA-prxp-75xx-3cxw / CVE-2025-5892 (moderate; 'RocketChat up to 7.6.1 ... parseMessage ... inefficient regular expression complexity'); no patched version published; the proposed fix PR #35711 is open and unmerged (GitHub API: state open, merged false); parseMessage.js:52-53 in 9.1.0-develop at 9f3d6c8c still holds the vulnerable expressions, so this version is affected. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-prxp-75xx-3cxw
findings.conditional_on: IRC_Enabled with a linked IRC server (the vendor marks the bridge not for production)
findings.impact: Low (CVSS 3.7): parseMessage tests each peer line with /^:|\s+:/ and then matches /(.*?)(?:^:|\s+:)(.*)/, and on a line that holds a long run of whitespace with no colon after it the \s+: alternative is retried from every position in the run, which is quadratic in the line's length. The receive loop puts no bound on either the buffer or a line: onReceiveFromPeer appends every chunk, splits on the line terminators, and parses each line, so one line of tens of thousands of spaces blocks Node's single thread for the duration of the backtracking and a stream of them keeps the event loop stalled, stopping the whole workspace rather than only the bridge. This is CVE-2025-5892, for which no patched version exists: the fix PR is still open.
findings.remediation: Parse linearly and bound the input. Replace the two expressions at parseMessage.js:52-53 with an indexOf(' :') (plus a leading-colon test) so the trailing parameter is split without backtracking, and enforce RFC 2813's 512-byte limit on both this.receiveBuffer and each line in onReceiveFromPeer (index.js:138-150), discarding anything longer. Grounding: deploy/knowledge/owasp/CheatSheetSeries/cheatsheets/Denial_of_Service_Cheat_Sheet.md (Input validation: bound the size of what a parser is given) with the analysis technique in deploy/knowledge/payloads/PayloadsAllTheThings/Regular Expression/README.md.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps the IRC bridge and removes only the weakness: a peer line longer than the protocol's own 512-byte limit is dropped instead of parsed, which is what RFC 2813 requires of a conforming implementation, so a non-conforming peer that sends over-long lines would lose those messages. The parser change is behaviour-preserving for every line within the limit.

findings.title: The email OTP attempt cap of RCSA-2023-0003 is read before the guess and written after it, so parallel guesses overrun it
findings.category: Brute force (check-then-update race on an attempt counter)
findings.status: FAILED (the race is real in shape (0 parallel guesses evaluated against 0 sequential before the cap), but it needs the victim's password first and widens a five-guess cap on a six-digit code: filtered under the brute-force rule, as the report has i)
findings.confidence_reasoning: The counter is read before the guess in source; the lab could not get an email code issued, so the race itself was not observed.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 08 R-07: residual of RCSA-2023-0003 (vendor security page; email OTP brute force, fixed 6.5.1 with an attempts counter); no tracker item; stage 04 noted the non-atomic counter among its pointers. https://docs.rocket.chat/docs/security-fixes-and-updates
findings.impact: Parallel guesses evaluate more than five email OTP codes per issued code.
findings.remediation: Increment the attempt counter atomically before comparing (findOneAndUpdate with attempts < cap) and refuse when the update matched nothing.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps email 2FA; concurrent guesses beyond the cap are refused.
findings.detail: Filtered (brute force): EmailCheck.ts:71-101 reads the attempt count, compares the code and runs bcrypt before incrementing, so a parallel burst evaluates more than the five guesses RCSA-2023-0003's cap intends; it still needs the victim's password first and still leaves a six-digit space per issued code. A human may re-open it together with the telemetry-settings increment, which can raise the cap outright.

findings.title: users.register answers Email already exists before it checks whether registration is open, a sibling of the enumeration CVE-2021-22892 closed
findings.category: Account enumeration (existence oracle)
findings.status: CONFIRMED (on a workspace with self-registration closed, an anonymous caller distinguishes an address that has an account from one that does not)
findings.confidence_reasoning: Proven by our own run against the pinned build; unauthenticated, default configuration.
findings.known_evidence: Stage 08 R-10: sibling of GHSA-7v8v-3xwh-j47p / CVE-2021-22892 (HackerOne #1089116; email enumeration, fixed < 3.12.2, 3.11.3, 3.13); no advisory or issue found for the register route. https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7v8v-3xwh-j47p
findings.impact: On deployments that closed self-registration, an anonymous caller learns whether an email or username has an account, at one probe per minute per address.
findings.remediation: Check whether registration is open before the availability checks and return one generic answer when it is closed.
findings.remediation_side_effects: Keeps registration; closed workspaces stop answering availability questions.
findings.detail: Filtered (enumeration): users.ts:984-997 answers 'Email already exists' or 'Username is already in use' before registerUser (:1011) refuses a Disabled or Secret URL registration form, so a closed-registration workspace still answers whether an address has an account, at one probe per minute per address. Sibling of CVE-2021-22892; a human may re-open it for SSO-only intranets, where the member list is the sensitive asset.

attack_chains.title: Anonymous takeover of Omnichannel customer conversations
attack_chains.steps: Register a visitor with a known customer's phone number to receive that customer's visitor token (VULN-001); or open one chat of your own and subscribe to any other Livechat room's message stream by naming your own room in extraData (VULN-076); with a stolen token, request the victim conversation's transcript to an attacker address (VULN-051).
attack_chains.impact: Unauthenticated read of customer conversations and impersonation of customers, plus delivery of their transcripts to the attacker, wherever Omnichannel is used.

attack_chains.title: Delegated integration role to server code execution
attack_chains.steps: A role holding only manage-incoming-integrations rewrites an existing outgoing integration's script through integrations.update type confusion, even via a request that fails validation (VULN-061); the script climbs from the serverFetch Reference to the host Function constructor (VULN-027).
attack_chains.impact: Code execution as the Rocket.Chat server process from a role that was meant to manage webhooks only.

attack_chains.title: Any user weakens the second factor, then guesses into accounts
attack_chains.steps: Harvest every address and role from users.listByStatus (VULN-007); raise Accounts_TwoFactorAuthentication_MaxDelta and the lockout thresholds through statistics.telemetry (VULN-057); guess passwords by email address, which skips the per-user lockout (VULN-032); a wide TOTP window then accepts most codes, and replayed codes stay valid (VULN-040).
attack_chains.impact: Account takeover of password-and-TOTP users, administrators included, starting from an ordinary account.

attack_chains.title: One leaked token becomes permanent account control
attack_chains.steps: Export a victim's resume token through ?loginClient=mobile to a program owning rocketchat:// (VULN-034); read the TOTP seed and backup-code hashes through users.info (VULN-004); keep a DDP socket open so the victim's password change or an admin reset does not end it, and receive the admin-set password in clear (VULN-033).
attack_chains.impact: A one-click token leak turns into durable account control that survives the standard remediation.

attack_chains.title: OAuth email meld into the env-created administrator
attack_chains.steps: With GitLab or a custom OAuth provider enabled, assert the administrator's address from an IdP account without verification (VULN-002); the env-created admin has no second factor, and young accounts skip 2FA on OAuth (VULN-043); a deactivated target is revived because the Passport path mints tokens without checking active (VULN-030).
attack_chains.impact: Administrator takeover of a fresh install that enabled an OAuth provider with unverified addresses.

attack_chains.title: CAS session fixation to persistent takeover
attack_chains.steps: Send a CAS user a link to the genuine CAS server carrying an attacker-chosen credential token and redeem it (VULN-044); read the TOTP seed with the new session (VULN-004); keep the socket alive across the victim's remediation (VULN-033).
attack_chains.impact: Takeover of any CAS user with one click, past Rocket.Chat's second factor, that persists.

attack_chains.title: Unauthenticated workspace outage
attack_chains.steps: Send long brace-led offline-form messages that drive the mailer's quadratic regex (VULN-073), grow the metrics registry with unique method.callAnon paths (VULN-074), and exhaust the shared anonymous rate-limit bucket so nobody can log in through the web client (VULN-078).
attack_chains.impact: A denial of service against every user from an anonymous client, combining CPU, memory and login availability.

attack_chains.title: Same-origin phishing with system authority
attack_chains.steps: Upload an HTML credential form and share its inline link on the workspace origin (VULN-021); announce it with a forged system notice through rooms.mediaConfirm (VULN-012) or, with visitor navigation messages on, a rocket.cat notice posted anonymously into any room (VULN-046).
attack_chains.impact: Credential phishing hosted on, and announced by, the workspace itself.

attack_chains.title: Pre-registered squat survives the owner's arrival
attack_chains.steps: Register a future colleague's address with a lure in the display name; the genuine verification mail carries it (VULN-042); after the owner signs in through OAuth, the attacker's sessions and PATs survive the meld (VULN-037).
attack_chains.impact: Hidden, persistent access to a colleague's account from the day they join.

attack_chains.title: Deleted content stays recoverable
attack_chains.steps: Read deleted thread roots through chat.syncThreadsList in the shipped configuration (VULN-059); with message history on, read every deleted and edited-away message through exports and chat.getMessage (VULN-049); with anonymous read on, serve those hidden messages to unauthenticated callers (VULN-047).
attack_chains.impact: Content users deliberately deleted, including credentials pasted by mistake, remains readable by members and, in some configurations, by anyone.

attack_chains.title: A banned member keeps the room
attack_chains.steps: After a ban, keep receiving the room's new messages as notifications and downloading its files (VULN-009); re-enter through a never-expiring invite created while a moderator (VULN-035); keep pushing forged userData and call events to the room's members (VULN-003).
attack_chains.impact: The ban, the moderators' tool to close a room to one person, does not close it.

attack_chains.title: A delegated Omnichannel role becomes the customer, then a standing export channel
attack_chains.steps: An agent holding only view-l-room reads another department's visitor tokens out of the navigation-history endpoint (VULN-077) and uses one to read and post in that conversation as the customer; a livechat-manager points the Livechat webhook at a listener with the SSRF guard still off, so every future conversation is posted there automatically (VULN-081); the transcript route then mails a chosen conversation to an attacker address (VULN-051).
attack_chains.impact: Customer impersonation across departments plus a retrying, log-legitimate export of every future Omnichannel conversation, from two non-admin Omnichannel roles.

quick_wins.fix: Allow-list the telemetry counter ids in updateStatsCounter.ts (the four the client sends): closes any-user writes to security settings.
Create a new visitor on a token miss instead of merging by phone or email, and project token out of the livechat/visitor response.
Drop jail.setSync('ivm', ivm) and expose serverFetch as a copy-only callback in buildSandbox.ts: closes the sandbox escape.
Add canAccessRoomIdAsync to chat.getDeletedMessages before the trash query.
Assign the escapeHtml result in sendTranscript.ts:164 and enforce Livechat_enable_transcript on the route.
Add the missing retentionOverrideGlobal validator (edit-room-retention-policy) to saveRoomSettings.
Add _hidden: { $ne: true } to the update queries of chat.syncThreadsList and chat.syncThreadMessages.
Stop validator 3 from swapping the requested room for extraData.rid in roomAccessValidator.compatibility.ts.
Build the self view of services in getFullUserData with the same allow-list /me uses.
Apply the parse-length cap and Message_MaxAllowedSize to attachment descriptions.
Key anonymous method-bridge limits on the client address and leave this.token unset without a header.
Refuse system message types in sendFileMessage as chat.sendMessage already does.
Call canAccessRoomAsync in findVisitedPages and pass projection: { 'navigation.token': 0 }, as findChatHistory already does.
Set ignoreSsrfValidation: false and pass allowList: settings.get('SSRF_Allowlist') on both Livechat webhook fetches, as PR #42201 did for triggers.
check(type, String) and check(name, String) at the top of getRoomByTypeAndName, and return error-invalid-room for both no match and no access.
Assign el.textContent instead of el.innerHTML in the composer's componentDidUpdate, and compare against innerText.
Fetch through serverFetch with the guard on in PendingFileImporter.downloadFile, as the sibling import fetch now does.

methodology:
**Scope.** Source analysed: `targets/rocket.chat/` at commit `9f3d6c8c48911e32ed6c2ce36befd431faa71190` (9.1.0-develop), the Meteor app, its packages (`packages/*`, `ee/packages/*`) and the Livechat widget. Library code in the lab image (Meteor accounts, isolated-vm, bad-words, prom-client) was read only to establish reachability and semantics. Inputs read in full: the manifest and `02_features.md` to `08_cve_regression.md` with the stage 02 feature-class files; stage 07's known-issue cross-check supplied every `known_status` and `known_evidence`.

**What was re-verified, and when.** On 2026-11-24 every finding's cited path was re-read at the pinned commit; where an earlier stage's line range was off, the corrected range is the one in `location` and in `findings/`. Every excerpt in `findings/VULN-NNN.md` is copied from the target by line range and checked against an anchor string, so a stale range fails the build. No request was sent to the lab in this stage.

**How to read statuses.** `CONFIRMED (source-traced: confirmed vulnerability; ...)` means the whole path is unambiguous in source; `CONFIRMED (source-traced: likely vulnerability; ...)` means the code path is clear but the effect depends on runtime behaviour (timing, a browser, a third party, a model) that stage 11 must observe. `NEEDS_MANUAL (...)` means the lab cannot provide the precondition; `manual_reason` names it (`other` is an Enterprise licence module: AI Search, SAML). `FAILED (filtered: ...)` is a Phase 2 filter with its reason in `detail`, overridable by a human; `INTENDED` cites the vendor document. `confirmed_at` stays blank until stage 11 reaches a verdict. Severity is always the CVSS 3.1 band of the vector (the engine enforces it), so several findings an earlier stage called Low are Medium here; where the realistic severity is lower, the finding's Impact says so. Confidence (1-10) scores whether it is a real, reportable vulnerability that matters; conditional findings are real for every deployment that enabled the feature.

**Filters applied (Phase 2).** Admin-only findings were filtered unless they reach code execution or a boundary the vendor treats as one: VULN-027 (sandbox escape), VULN-014 and VULN-075 (run-import file read and SSRF, matching the vendor's own GHSA-6x96 for that permission) and VULN-061/VULN-069 (delegated roles) were kept; VULN-025 was filtered. Brute force and rate limiting: VULN-016, VULN-063, VULN-065 (rate-limit leg) and VULN-083 filtered; VULN-032 kept because it defeats a documented per-account lockout, VULN-078 because the shared bucket is a denial of service. Enumeration: VULN-084 filtered; VULN-079 kept (operator injection that extracts private names without guessing). Theoretical: VULN-029 (no oracle: every SAML failure ends in the same redirect).
